passage: Monday evening. Tarun laid out coloured pens, sticky flags and a fresh planner. Boards were seven weeks away. He coloured the Physics notes in four shades. Tuesday evening. He flagged every chapter, sorted the flags by colour and admired the planner: it looked like a magazine. Wednesday evening. Anirban messaged, "Which chapter did you finish?" Tarun looked at the neat desk and the untouched books. None. He typed, "Almost," and put his phone face down. His chest was tight, the fear he had been decorating over for three days. He opened the Physics book to chapter one and read the first paragraph three times, because his hands were not steady.

qa.q: What did Tarun do on Tuesday evening?
qa.a: He flagged every chapter, sorted the flags by colour and admired the planner.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when he typed "Almost"?
qa.a: Anxious and a bit ashamed, since he had avoided the truth and his chest was tight.

qa.q: What could Tarun do to break the pattern?
qa.a: Study one small chapter for twenty minutes without decorating, tick it off and tell Anirban, because starting shrinks the fear.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Tarun's reply?
qa.a: As vague, since Anirban asked a simple question and got "Almost", and may sense that something is wrong.

grounding: A student spends three evenings on colour-coding and planners without studying a chapter, so the fear underneath stays untouched.

passage: Sangeeta, making a timetable again? Sit, let me tell you about your Irfan Uncle in Class 10. Three evenings before the prelims, I came home with a pack of coloured flags and six gel pens. First evening, I rewrote my Chemistry notes in four colours. Second evening, I flagged every page. Third evening, I made a planner so pretty that my Ammi showed it to the neighbours. I felt so busy. But I hadn't opened one chapter I didn't already know. The truth was, organic chemistry frightened me, and colouring was a way to sit near it without touching it. The night before the paper, I finally opened that chapter and every page was new. I failed that prelim, beta. With very pretty flags.

qa.q: How many gel pens did young Irfan come home with?
qa.a: Six gel pens, along with a pack of coloured flags.

qa.q: What was young Irfan really feeling underneath all the colouring?
qa.a: Young Irfan was frightened of organic chemistry, and colouring let him feel busy while avoiding it.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story could have changed the prelim result?
qa.a: Opening the organic chemistry chapter on the first evening instead of rewriting notes, because facing the scary chapter early would have left time to learn it.

qa.q: How might Ammi have felt showing the planner to the neighbours?
qa.a: Ammi was proud, thinking the pretty planner meant hard work, which shows how convincing the organising looked from outside.

grounding: An elder recalls spending three evenings colouring notes and making a planner while the feared chapter stayed unstudied.

passage: The board exams were three weeks away, and Devika's house was full of relatives for her cousin Aparna's wedding: dholak every night, cousins sleeping on every mattress. Studying felt impossible, so Devika found a corner of the terrace and organised instead. First evening, she rewrote her Economics notes in pastel highlighters. Second evening, she stuck colour-coded flags into every textbook. Third evening, she built a planner with decorative tape and tiny stickers. It looked like something from a shop. On the fourth night Aparna climbed up with two cups of chai and flipped through it. "Beautiful. Which chapters have you done?" Devika opened her mouth and shut it. None. She had flagged the Accounts book twice and not read a page of it, and her stomach dropped the way it always did near Accounts.

qa.q: Where did Devika work during the wedding?
qa.a: In a corner of the terrace.

qa.q: What does Devika's stomach dropping near Accounts suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she was afraid of Accounts, and the organising let her dodge that fear while feeling busy.

qa.q: What would you change first for Devika?
qa.a: Put the planner aside and spend the next evening on one Accounts chapter, even with the noise, since facing the feared subject is the real work.

qa.q: How might Aparna see the planner?
qa.a: Aparna admires it, but by asking which chapters are done, gently shows that a beautiful planner is not the same as studying.

grounding: Shows a student spending three evenings organising notes and a planner during a noisy wedding while the feared subject stays unstudied.
